bugs.summary: The PR flips the commit/PR-title rule to Conventional Commits but leaves the linear-issue-workflow skill's PR-title rule banning `feat:`/scope prefixes, so an agent following that skill writes PR titles that the new CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md say will be declined.
bugs.evidence: At head plugins/corbits-skills/skills/linear-issue-workflow/SKILL.md:182 (unchanged) under '### PR title shape': "`style`'s commit-subject rules apply: start with a verb, no leading prefix (no `feat:`, no `[scope]`, no ticket ID)". The same PR rewrites CONTRIBUTING.md:153-158 to require `<type>(<scope>): <description>` PR titles, AGENTS.md:69-70 'A pull request that violates CONTRIBUTING.md will be declined', and updated the sibling implement/review/style skills and builder prompt, but missed this one. The stale line was later removed in 3ae50a4f (refactor(skills): fold the ship loop and integration rules into implement and review).

rejected.was: bake-off cluster (~10 prompts): AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md state 'a violating pull request is declined' as settled while the PR says enforcement is undecided
rejected.why: The open question in the PR is the mechanism (review norm vs CI title check), not whether violating PRs are declined; the docs state the rule, which is the PR's purpose. Wording of policy docs, not a defect.

rejected.was: bake-off cluster (~10 prompts): CONTRIBUTING.md states release-note generation from merged PRs as current fact
rejected.why: The PR declares the dependency on #984 and is a coordinated docs change; a sequencing note in documentation is not a defect in this change.

rejected.was: bake-off cluster (7 prompts): style SKILL.md:105 'Match what is there' (capitalization of recent history) conflicts with the new Conventional Commits rule
rejected.why: The sentence covers verb tense, detail, voice and capitalization; the explicit Conventional Commits format immediately below governs the prefix and the PR states earlier history keeps its old form. A wording nuance in an agent skill, no incorrect behaviour shown.

rejected.was: bake-off cluster (4 prompts: 00, 08, 24, 13): lowercase-description rule vs 'only type and scope are new' / history voice
rejected.why: Same wording nuance as above; documentation consistency, not a defect.

rejected.was: bake-off findings (2 prompts: 18, 23): runtime prompt in src/agent/directors/builder/package.ts:84 changed under a 'docs only' claim
rejected.why: The prompt text updates the builder's commit-style instruction to the new rule, consistent with the change; a description wording issue, not a defect.

rejected.was: bake-off findings (2 prompts: 10, 19): the PR's own title does not follow the rule it introduces
rejected.why: Explicitly intended: the PR says its own commits were rewritten to the rule as it stands before merge.

rejected.was: round2 findings (v-sweep-high, composite-medium, v-code-field-high, v-grounding-high): the eight rewritten open branches will be declined under the new binding rule / no grandfather clause
rejected.why: Intended: the PR says the rewrite keeps them compliant with the rule in force when they merge and that new work uses the scoped form after this lands; CONTRIBUTING.md:106 says older log entries keep their old form.

rejected.was: findings (bakeoff 13, round2 v-code-field-medium): CONTRIBUTING drops 'match the voice of recent history' while the style skill still says match the log
rejected.why: Same wording nuance as the style SKILL.md:105 cluster; the explicit Conventional Commits rule governs the form.

rejected.was: findings (round2 composite-high, v-sweep-high, bakeoff 22, 24): type list omits `revert`; review skill would flag git's default Revert/Merge subjects
rejected.why: The closed type list is a deliberate policy choice; Conventional Commits 1.0.0 does not require `revert`. Speculative audit noise, not a defect in this change.
Wording/judgment of a policy doc, no incorrect behaviour.

rejected.was: findings (bakeoff 05, round2 00-consensus-medium, v-no-speculation-exclusion-high): banned `(security):` status tag collides with a valid `fix(security):` scope
rejected.why: Kept verbatim from the old rule as a status tag in place of a type; wording ambiguity in a doc, and the review skill's status-tag check lists only `WIP:`/`[urgent]`, so no tool misbehaves.

rejected.was: round2 v-grounding-medium: type list copied into CONTRIBUTING, style and review skills
rejected.why: Maintainability/style; the copies agree at head.

rejected.was: round2 findings (v-no-speculation-exclusion-high, v-grounding-medium): review skill does not flag a missing scope that CONTRIBUTING and style require
rejected.why: Scope may be omitted when a change spans the repo, a judgment the audit leaves to the reviewer; the review skill is lenient, not wrong.

rejected.was: CONTRIBUTING.md:215 (unchanged) 'so the title stays a plain-English sentence' left in the Linear section
rejected.why: Stale wording only; it advises keeping ticket IDs out of the title, which still holds, and instructs nothing that violates the new rule.
